scope: Same-machine clean-rebuild reproducibility check of the fully native standard debug APK; entry-set/content/ordering/alignment/signing comparison of the build committed at 95ecbf62 versus one clean rebuild of the same source state.

source_apk.built_by: native-rebuild task-5 (2026-10-21T19:12:42+01:00), fully native rebuild after cargo clean

content_differences.observation: same uncompressed size, different content hash/CRC; consistent with non-deterministic dex merging/ordering
same uncompressed size, different content hash/CRC
same uncompressed size, different content hash/CRC
same uncompressed size, 53,645 differing bytes between the two builds (source-vs-rebuild), consistent with non-deterministic native build metadata/build-id; root cause not isolated

conclusion: A clean rebuild of the identical source state on the same machine is NOT byte-for-byte reproducible: the APK differs in size, in four entry contents (three dex files and libcrypto.so) and in ZIP local-entry ordering/alignment padding, while the entry set, uncompressed sizes, signing scheme/certificate and 16 KB alignment validity are unchanged. Byte-for-byte APK reproducibility across machines is therefore not established; the differences are localized to non-deterministic dex/native-build content plus packaging order/padding.
limitations: Two builds on one machine only; no cross-machine/cross-JDK comparison.
libcrypto.so byte differences were not root-caused (build-id/timestamps/compiler nondeterminism candidates); no file-level investigation beyond byte-count.
The APK is debug-signed; release signing and distribution reproducibility are not covered.
No functional equivalence claim beyond identical entry set and identical uncompressed sizes.
The rebuild used the same source tree and did not change app/Gradle inputs; only caches were cleared.
no_overclaims: This receipt records build-output non-determinism only. It does not claim a functional defect, a release-signing result, or reproducibility on another machine.

correction_2026-10-22.reason: The earlier comparison described the two APKs as built from the "identical source state"; that is true for app/ source content but not for the git revision/BUILD_ID. Root-cause analysis (2026-10-22) separated build-input differences from build nondeterminism.
findings: libcrypto.so: genuine same-input build nondeterminism but semantically benign — only .rodata/.text/.rela.dyn differ, caused solely by OpenSSL util/mkbuildinf.pl embedding the build timestamp; .comment/.note.android.ident/dynsym/dynstr/.gnu.*/headers are identical; differing instructions are same-address/same-mnemonic with only immediates shifted by the moved .rodata string (address fix-ups).

classes16/23/30.dex: NOT nondeterminism. The source APK was built at commit 63a2bbb3 and the rebuild at 95ecbf62 (embedded BUILD_ID differs); app/ source is identical between the commits, and only BuildConfig plus two classes that inline BUILD_ID change, with D8 per-dex checksum-map churn shifting later DEX data by one byte.

ZIP layout / 4,874,972-byte size delta: benign incremental-packaging history (holes/padding reuse); 1,634/1,638 entries keep identical local offsets and only the four changed entries moved into prior holes.
correction_2026-10-22.mitigations: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for the OpenSSL ExternalProject; pin BUILD_ID (or build both from the same commit); clean app/build + packaging intermediates before compared builds; keep the toolchain pinned. A follow-up experiment builds twice with those inputs to demonstrate (or bound) byte reproducibility.
correction_2026-10-22.conclusion_update: The observed APK difference was not proof of general build nondeterminism: one component is a benign timestamp string, one is a build-input (BUILD_ID) difference, and one is packaging history. Cross-machine/release-signing reproducibility remains out of scope.
